content.title: About
content.content: Tea, iced, brewed, black, unsweetened is a refreshing beverage made from black tea leaves brewed with hot water and then chilled. It contains no added sugar, preserving the natural bitterness and aroma of black tea while being low in calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black tea is the most consumed tea worldwide after green tea.
Cooling brewed tea retains most antioxidants such as polyphenols.
Iced tea is often served with a slice of lemon or lime to enhance flavor.
Unlike many ready‑to‑drink beverages, iced brewed tea contains no preservatives or artificial flavors.
The term “iced tea” originated in the United States in the early 20th century and quickly became a summer staple.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Black tea provides polyphenols that help combat free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Regular consumption of black tea may help lower LDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: Improved focus
items.content: Caffeine in black tea boosts alertness and cognitive performance.

items.title: Sugar‑free hydration
items.content: Unsweetened iced tea supplies fluid without extra calories.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Tannins in black tea can help regulate digestion and reduce bloating.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: People sensitive to caffeine may experience nervousness, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Iron absorption
items.content: Tannins can reduce the absorption of non‑heme iron from plant foods, so it’s best to drink tea between meals.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Frequent consumption may increase stomach acidity in individuals with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the iced brewed black tea chilled over ice. Optionally add a slice of lemon, lime, or fresh mint. If desired, sweeten lightly with honey or stevia, but the classic version contains no added sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared iced tea in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Discard if it becomes cloudy, develops an off‑taste, or smells stale.
